content.text: This clause meets the preferred position on every material term.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Sections 8.2 and 8.3 satisfy the preferred position in full: renewal terms are twelve months (not multi-year), Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, Vendor must send a reminder sixty days before renewal (with the opt-out deadline extended if it fails to do so — a mechanic that favours us), and renewal uplift is capped at the lesser of US CPI and three percent with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The notice window and price cap are well inside both the preferred and fallback thresholds, so no redline is warranted.
